Iain: See Ian, although the weird ‘i’ in the middle of his name provides him with more academic potential, a more forthright business stance and a slightly larger ego.
Ian: The sound of a teaspoon being dropped onto a tiled floor. The ungainly twang is noisy without being painful and more often than not it leaves a mess, but did you ever stop and study the shape of the pattern of the mess? Check it out next time. You might be surprised to discover the artist that lies within. Suffice to say if Ian is ever undergoing some kind of existential crisis you’ll never know about it unless he tells you.
Ib: Regardless of where he is from (and if it’s not a nickname then he must be Danish or something) Ib bounces along with a cheerful grin, as if he’s a basketball having escaped the court via an errant shot and is now merrily bouncing his way down a steep hill towards a busy intersection. Ib doesn’t give a fuck. He just wants to have fun and hang out with as many cool, bouncing people as possible, and busy intersections are generally full of them. Amen.
Ignatius: Every moment, event and deed in his life presents as an opportunity for good-natured competition. It can be painful after a while and his partners tend to be very patient. Usually, however, Ignatius is good fun and he provides a non-boring setting.
Igor: Igor is more light-hearted than you think but do yourself a favour and don’t even pretend that you want to fight him. It’s a Croatian thing...
Ijad:
“Ijad! Fuck, look out!” screams his panic-stricken friend, pointing desperately at the ground beneath Ijad’s feet. “Snaaaaake!”

Ijad calmly stops in his tracks and looks down. True enough a deadly adder is curled up and beginning to stir next to his sandals. Without even looking up, Ijad raises an open palm in the direction of his friend, silencing further outbursts. When he understands the snake is okay, he raises his eyes to his pal and quietly smiles.

“Relax,” Ijad whispers. “He’s cool.”

And day by day, Ijad knows that one day his friend will be too.

The end.
Ike:
Ike crashes his helicopter and is badly injured. A rescuer arrives late and very calmly Ike says to them, “No, I’m done. Now leave me be.” 
Ike.
Ilias: Ilias is a medical name for a medical man in that he computes information very quickly and, by and large, very well.
Ilman: Ilman is a sufficiently savvy operator. He is generally educated enough to not only know the rules, but to occasionally deliberately break them, although not if it means hurting others in any way. (Wasteful government departments notwithstanding.) His kids treat him as if he is a playful teenager, himself, and he aspires to keep life simple and happy. In the bedroom he is as kinky as you'd expect.
Imron: Imron is a bloody twit sometimes. Sure, he's a funny, goofy guy who everyone likes and for good reason - he's generous with his time, he loves animals and kids and he loves the outdoors - but his capacity to think laterally on any level is completely missing. If he ever read one of those prank newspapers that regularly interviews alien abductees he'd be on the next plane to Area 51 and God knows where else, in search of aliens. Imron, just because you read it doesn't make it true, mate.
Indi: I swear Steven Spielberg altered a generation. Anyway, Indi is a nice young man just trying to get by in a giant, over-complicated world that is becoming more like Big Brother everyday. Indi yearns for the quiet life more than most and he's not sure what he wants from life just yet, so don't push him. Time - what he wants is a bit more time to figure it out.
Indiana: Drinks a hot soy skinny latte and lives in the city.
Indigo:
Is he a shoemaker?
No. Not enough stimuli.
Is he a fighter pilot?
No way. His maths isn’t up to it, or maybe he just never got into it, and he isn’t the toughest in the group under pressure.
Is an artist?
Mmmm, sometimes, yep, even though he kind of loathes the cliché.
Is he a muso’?
Occasionally, yes, and a fine one. Anyway, forget the Q&A, what’s important to know is that Indigo is a borderline hippie, but not so much that he hasn’t organised himself in a Western world. And he’d make a fine dad, and what better job is there?
(PS- he’d actually be wonderful working with wood. Is he doing that? Anyone?...)
Ingo: Ingo has drunk at the same pub every afternoon for 25 years. He seems to have avoided a life of responsibilty and at a very impressionable 50 years of age he still thinks he's a bloody teenager.
Innes: Innes is the opposite of incompetent. And he has a sense of humour. Don’t let any of his staff try to convince you otherwise.
Ion: A welcoming smile heralds an open-minded yet conservative-looking fellow. Sounds contradictory, I know. Rarely impulsive, Ion's car is well-serviced and the log book meticulously maintained, which, gleefully, is exactly the opposite of his sex life which, while organised, is full of kink, unpredictability and bizarre personalities. Go hard son!
Irfan: Irfan excels at finding simple solutions to seemingly complex problems.
Irvin: Irvin looks like a gum tree but he's actually a fern.
Irving: The men in the trenches are dour. Fear strangles their stomachs and all of them know that very few of them will be alive in ten minutes. Can you believe humans do such things to each other? Anyway, Irving is no different, except perhaps he is. “Oh well, fuck this,” he says. “If we're really going over the top, at least let me tell you blokes this joke I heard yesterday….” Irving.
Isaac: You’ll often find his picture in the social pages where he is generally surrounded by beautiful women who seem to be having the time of their lives.
Isher: Bank Manager. And he's at the beginning of his own little corporate mission.
Ismail: Well-schooled and watchful of his possessions, Ismail is like a very shiny rock crystal which is fun to hold and observe, but who gives away nothing as to how he was constructed (or what he might be thinking).
Itchy: The highly intelligent and fast-moving gymnast. Perpetually ready for just about everything.
Iva: If Iva were born in India, and we can virtually assure you that he isn’t, although who knows what happens in past life events, he would never be of a lower caste. Not that any notion of social status enters his head of course, for Iva is a clear-headed, eminently-present and generous individual. No, he doesn’t work with his hands and the graceful lines of his name forever propel him into a genial, artistic life which is as subdued as it is brilliant. He’s another one of these fathers who infuriates his young children (and partners, occasionally) because he simply refuses to be drawn into any kind of petty, quarrelling melodrama.
Ivan: Ivan believes that everything in the world exists inside well-defined black and white squares.
Ivo: No, Ivo isn’t evil, he’s just a man trying to look and act like a man in a world where men are being urged to behave very correctly.
Ivor: Ivor keeps hearing voices behind  him. The upshot is that if you are ever talking to him, you can see that he's only partially listening. He's not being rude, trust me, he's just trying to figure out what's going on behind him. (He's written off several cars for the same reason.)
Izaak:
He's a funny fellow alright. Taken to flights of fancy quite easily, one minute you'll see him rushing off to helicopter school until he realises he's scared of heights. The next you'll find him blazing out to sea in his new career of deep-sea fisherman. Yes, he spent tens of thousands of dollars on a boat and fishing gear, but did he ever try and find out if got sea sick? Of course not. Now look at him - throwing his guts up all down the side of his big white boat and he's barely left the bloody harbour. 
Izaak, some advice lad: this here is the address of the local Buddhist temple. I want you to go there, sit down and just relax for a moment. There’s no rush, so close your eyes for a wee while and see if  you can discover what it is you truly desire.
Izzy: As a funny, smart and charismatic bastard, Izzy is irrepressible.
